title: The evidence bar in clinical AI: what Brainomix and DeepHealth set
subtitle: The market's winners won on breadth, workflow, or evidence
excerpt: Clinical AI adoption in the NHS still stalls on alert fatigue, opaque single scores, bypassable oversight, cloud-only outages, and thin real-world evidence.
content:
What the evidence bar now looks like

Clinical AI adoption in the NHS still stalls on alert fatigue, opaque single scores, bypassable oversight, cloud-only outages, and thin real-world evidence. Brainomix's Lancet Digital Health study and DeepHealth/Kheiron's GEMINI study show what the evidence bar now looks like. These are the templates any platform must meet to convert a strong architecture into regulated, evidenced, deployed reality.

Brainomix's study — 452,952 patients across 107 NHS hospitals — demonstrated that AI-assisted triage doubled the rate of endovascular treatment for stroke (from 2.3% to 4.6%) and reduced door-in-door-out time by 64 minutes. DeepHealth/Kheiron's GEMINI study — 10,889 women — demonstrated a 10.4% increase in cancer detection with over 30% workload reduction and 47 additional interval cancers detected.
author: Dolapo Ariyo

evidence.claim: Brainomix Lancet DH 2025: 452,952 patients, 107 NHS hospitals, EVT doubled
DeepHealth/Kheiron GEMINI in Nature Cancer Mar 2026: 10,889 women, +10.4% detection
SEWA evidence pathway: shadow trial → NIHR EME → UKCA Class IIb
